title: From the Editor — Dead Weight in the Basin
settingText: Cinder Basin seen from high and far: pale basin floor, heat shimmer, a small patchwork traveling camp beneath black half-buried Sunforge ribs. The road arrives from the lower corner. No identifiable faces; the visual should feel like a place already waiting.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 2. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One wrong name can be an accident.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By the time Brandon Mack leaves the Last Drop, the accident has acquired witnesses, enemies, a hero, and a road of its own.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He has also acquired Jessie and Eva, though he may dispute the wording.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Out here, stories move faster than people, and a reputation does not need permission from the person wearing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A camp there has been waiting a long time for somebody.

directionInline.text: This is an interior editorial/interstitial comic page, not a cover or dossier. Preserve the grounded Sunforge Outlaw visual world: hard Sunfields light, tactile dust, worn materials, ordinary frontier life, strong silhouettes and no generic cyberpunk.

The supplied lettering is exact production text. If a generation pass cannot render long body copy reliably, preserve the successful artwork with a clean reserved text field and correct the lettering separately rather than changing or shortening the copy.
No spoilers beyond what the supplied editorial text itself implies. Do not visually reveal the next issue's identity mistake, confrontation, culprit, resolution or other first-page surprise.

title: Five Days South
summary: After several days on the road, the trio arrives at a lived-in Cinder Basin settlement; their reasons for stopping are ordinary.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE WIDE road panel: hard white light, pale dry ground and glassed patches. Jessie's worn rig crawls along a ridge, passing black half-buried physical Sunforge ribs used as shade by distant workers. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “Five days south of the Last Drop, Brandon Mack was still going away.”  Brandon: “How much farther?”

Panel 2 — TIGHT two-shot inside the rig. Jessie's hand steadies the wheel as a loose canvas tie squeaks; Eva has her worn notebook on her lap, with no readable marks. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “Until we find water.”  Eva: “You told him that an hour ago.”  Jessie: “Still true.”

Panel 3 — TALL reveal downhill into Cinder Basin: family tents under patched canvas shade attached to inert black Sunforge ribs, food on fires, tethered mounts and ordinary camp work. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “Cinder Basin had water. It also had Los Lagartos.”  Jessie: “There.”
Panel 4 — BOTTOM inset: Brandon watches people gathering around a dinner fire, not yet aware they are noticing him. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “Looks busy.”

dialogueInline.text: Five days south of the Last Drop, Brandon Mack was still going away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You told him that an hour ago.

title: A Camp with Its Own Business
summary: Introduce Los Lagartos through everyday relationships and work; Pilar cooks, Rosa and Mateo disagree and Nico follows Mateo.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE WIDE of a functional family camp. Pilar, older gray braid and patched red apron, hands a pot down the table. Rosa, dark curls under faded green headwrap, helps a child adjust a harness. Mateo, stocky middle-aged man in dark canvas vest, argues quietly by the fire. Nico, slim young adult in ocher scarf with an ordinary holstered pistol, stands with him. Black ribs hold shade cloth and blankets. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “They were a traveling people. They had been arguing long before the rig arrived.”
Panel 2 — LIVELY small inset: Eva hops down by children; Jessie tugs at the same loose canvas tie. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “Do they sell food?”  Jessie: “Ask before you eat it.”

Panel 3 — MEDIUM on Rosa and Mateo beside stacks of bowls and blankets; affection and irritation coexist. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Rosa: “You promised to bring everyone to supper.”  Mateo: “I'm here.”  Rosa: “I can see you.”

Panel 4 — LOW panel by water tins: Brandon climbs out, removing hat and wiping dust. Pilar catches sight of him; her ladle stops halfway to a bowl. Lighting and matter stay mundane. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Pilar: “...General?”

title: General Diaz
summary: Pilar identifies Brandon as Diaz. Camp responses diverge; Brandon supplies his own name without theatrics.

Panel 2 — MEDIUM on Brandon holding his hat beside the water table; Pilar steps toward him. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “My name is Brandon Mack.”  Pilar: “You took your time.”  Brandon: “I'm sorry, but you have the wrong man.”

Panel 3 — THREE-WAY depth: Pilar uncertain but glad, Mateo indignant, Rosa looking for some evidence. Eva pays attention to the people. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Mateo: “He doesn't get to walk back in here like this.”  Rosa: “You don't even know if it's him.”
Panel 4 — NARROW near rig: Jessie picks up two empty water tins and turns toward the exit, practical, not scared. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “I'll fill these.”  Brandon: “Please do.”

title: Water Before History
summary: Pilar offers hospitality while the other Lagartos attempt to recruit Brandon into old arguments.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE water table: Pilar fills a dented tin cup for Brandon. People continue eating behind them. Mateo and Nico remain at a visible distance, Nico's holstered pistol at his hip. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Pilar: “Drink. You always came in thirsty.”  Brandon: “Thank you.”
Panel 2 — CLOSE on Pilar, more moved than certain. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Pilar: “It has been years.”  Brandon: “Then I think you'd know him better than I would.”

Panel 3 — CROPPED reverse on Mateo and Nico at the edge of the same table. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Mateo: “If you came to put things right, say it in front of everyone.”  Brandon: “I only stopped for water.”
Panel 4 — QUIET two-shot Eva and Brandon. She has noticed Rosa listening from the edge. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “You didn't ask what things.”  Brandon: “I expect I'll hear.”

title: The Argument Was Already There
summary: Rosa won a community vote; Mateo believes Diaz's old authority should favor his family's claim. Distinct personal stakes, no procedural exposition.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE UNEVEN meal-table geometry. Some members sit on either side, others circulate with bowls. Rosa and Mateo are arguing as people who know each other, not in a hearing. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Rosa: “They chose me.”  Mateo: “While Diaz was gone.”  Rosa: “He was gone when they chose you to speak for him, too.”

Panel 2 — TIGHT on Mateo. Nico stands behind him, a younger man's frustration visible. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Mateo: “My father rode with Diaz for twenty years.”  Rosa: “Your father isn't the one asking to lead us.”

Panel 3 — INSERT of worn repaired head chair at one end of an ordinary table. Pilar touches its back; nothing ceremonial glows or bears inscriptions. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Pilar: “We kept his place.”  Brandon: “You can keep it.”
Panel 4 — SMALL final observation: Eva watches two members whisper angrily, then pass a bowl between them anyway. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “The quarrel was real. So was supper.”

title: The General's Chair
summary: People attempt to seat Brandon in Diaz's chair. An ordinary dull-metal token changes hands and is returned visibly.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — TALL panel: two Lagartos steer Brandon toward the repaired head chair as he tries to take a seat elsewhere. He remains calm and polite. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Pilar: “Please. Sit here.”  Brandon: “I would rather sit with everybody else.”

Panel 2 — CLOSE hands: Pilar places an old plain dull-metal token in Brandon's open palm, then withdraws. The token bears no mysterious mark and proves nothing about him. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Pilar: “He left this with us.”  Brandon: “Then it belongs with you.”

Panel 3 — WIDE side-on: Brandon slides the head chair aside. Mateo and Rosa watch with conflicting interpretations. Nico remains behind Mateo. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Mateo: “Is that your answer?”  Brandon: “It's a chair.”

Panel 4 — LOW small insert: Brandon places the token beside Pilar's bowl, clearly returning it, while someone quietly shifts the chair back. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “Nobody had asked Brandon to be himself.”

title: A Way Out
summary: Jessie prepares to depart; Sand Rider and Nico's physical weapon are established before the confrontation.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE camp edge: Jessie refills water tins and fastens the squeaking rig tie. Sand Rider—lean, plainly human, sun goggles, wrapped face and layered canvas—walks his weary mount into view. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “We have enough water.”

Panel 2 — THREE-SHOT at rig, Brandon still holding cup. Eva watches the table. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “They're arguing about whether they have to listen to somebody who isn't here.”  Jessie: “And they've decided somebody who isn't him should settle it.”

Panel 3 — MEDIUM past Sand Rider, face briefly visible with goggles raised. Nico storms toward Mateo with his plain sidearm still fully holstered. The scout notices. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Sand Rider: “That boy has been waiting to lose his temper since breakfast.”  Brandon: “Which boy?”

Panel 4 — NARROW panel: Jessie and Eva look back toward the table. Jessie's grip on the rig rail shows she intends to go. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “The one with a gun. We leave before dark.”  Eva: “I haven't even eaten.”

title: A Name in the Dust
summary: Eva reports the verified facts. Raina watches their exit; the trio has evidence of advance knowledge but no definitive explanation.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE moving rig down the Cinder Basin road. Eva catches rear rail and climbs in, Jessie steering. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “A preacher got here three days before us.”  Jessie: “And?”

Panel 2 — MEDIUM inside moving rig; Eva looks to both companions for reactions. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “He told them black hair, dark coat, and that Brandon would deny being Diaz.”  Jessie: “That last part is new.”  Brandon: “It still doesn't tell us why.”

Panel 3 — NARROW from Jessie's shoulder. Eva begins to object; Brandon listens instead of dismissing her. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “You think he guessed?”  Brandon: “I don't know.”  Jessie: “Neither do I.”

Panel 4 — VERY WIDE rearward panel through natural dust. Raina watches from beside an inert half-buried black Sunforge rib at the narrowing camp road. She stays human and grounded; Brandon does not look back. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “A wrong name had followed Brandon out of the Last Drop. This time, somebody had reached the next one first.”
